title: Offline strategy is write-buffer by default with elicited alternatives for read-only-banner and refuse-writes
context: Applications differ on what they want to do while offline. A note-taking application wants a write-buffer so the operator keeps working. A financial application wants to refuse writes altogether because a queued write against stale server state is worse than a hard fail. A dashboard application wants a read-only banner and refuses writes silently. There is no single sensible default; the shelf blueprint commits to one and elicits the two alternatives.
decision: Default is write-buffer per TAC-2303: writes queue to IndexedDB with an idempotency token and flush on reconnection with server-side dedupe. Elicited alternatives are read-only-banner (the surface renders a banner and every write control disables) and refuse-writes (every write attempt fails locally with a clear message; nothing queues). The elicited answer lives on the applied-blueprint sidecar and the state machine reads it on offline entry. elicited is true; recommendedDefault stays false because the choice is genuinely per-project.
consequences: Projects that want the write-buffer get the default with no configuration; the pack drives an offline probe and asserts window.__offlineBuffer is populated. Projects electing read-only-banner get a simpler UI at the cost of losing the operator's in-flight writes. Projects electing refuse-writes get the strictest posture with the clearest failure mode. All three shapes render the offline region and the polite reconnection announcement per REQ-005; the difference is only whether writes queue, disable or refuse.

alternativesConsidered.name: Force refuse-writes as the default
alternativesConsidered.summary: Refuse every offline write locally; no buffer; no queue.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Loses the operator's in-flight work every time the network drops for a few seconds; the most common failure mode (transient loss) becomes the most painful.

alternativesConsidered.name: Server-side sync engine
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ship a CRDT or event-sourced sync engine as part of this blueprint.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Outside the shelf blueprint's scope (this is a UI-state blueprint, not a persistence blueprint); belongs to a future persistence-sync-engine blueprint if the shelf grows one.
